biography.plain_text: William Kissam Vanderbilt II was an American railroad heir, racing driver and founder of the Vanderbilt Cup. Educated at St. Mark's and Harvard, he helped establish the Long Island Motor Parkway with fellow investors. Known as Willie K., he inherited a substantial fortune from his father and settled in Centerport, New York.

long_biography.plain_text:
Railroad heir William Kissam Vanderbilt II assembled a natural-history collection through ocean expeditions. He worked with scientists from the American Museum of Natural History to catalogue marine specimens and published a research bulletin. His collecting ranged from fish and invertebrates to shells, birds and cultural objects from Africa and the South Pacific.

He opened the Hall of Fishes to visitors in 1922, initially one day a week and by appointment. As his collections grew, he added a second floor. His will provided for the Centerport estate to become a public museum after his wife's lifetime, supported by an endowment.
